text:
alyssa: heads-up — multiple customers reporting console graphs not loading. tiles spin and network tab shows 500 from /api/v1/analytics/query. first reports ~08:32 UTC. no recent frontend deploys AFAIK. affected: acme-logistics-prod, beta-retailer. some requests succeed, ~5-10% hit 500s. attaching quick repro steps below.

support-jordan: can you paste a failing request id / curl and the response body? also which dashboard/time-range you used?

alyssa: repro steps: 1) open dashboard -> last 7d, 2) click tile -> request to /api/v1/analytics/query. curl we used (token redacted):
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"SELECT ...","range":{"from":"2026-03-16T00:00:00Z","to":"2026-03-16T08:00:00Z"}}' \
  https://console.redwood.inference/api/v1/analytics/query -D -
```
response headers include: X-Request-ID: req_02b7f3c4 and status 500. body: `{"error":"internal error","code":"INTERNAL"}`.

eng-analytics-maya: looking at analytics-api, I'm seeing repeated stack traces around that request id. snippet from logs (08:31:12 -> 08:33:00 UTC):
```
2026-03-16T08:31:12Z [req_02b7f3c4] ERROR QueryQueueTimeout: waited 30s in queue, queue_length=1189
2026-03-16T08:31:12Z [req_02b7f3c4] ERROR Handler failing with 500 internal
2026-03-16T08:31:13Z WARN queue_length spike: 880 -> 1200 in 30s
```
It looks like the analytics query worker pool is saturated and requests are timing out while waiting in the internal queue. not a parsing error.

ops-ryan: correlating infra metrics: clickhouse write-latency p99 jumped to 3.2s at 08:30 and batch ingestion lag increased. that caused backpressure to the aggregator which pushed work into analytics query queue. alert fired: analytics-query-queue > 1000. (sre-bot posted the alert).

sre-bot: Alert: analytics-query-queue.size > 1000 (triggered at 2026-03-16T08:30:58Z).

eng-ml: quick mitigation ideas: - route console queries to read-replica with throttling - increase analytics-api workers to drain queue - add fast-fail (503) for queries over threshold so the frontend can fallback to placeholder tiles instead of blocking.

alyssa: customers asking for ETA. any short term fix we can roll now?

eng-analytics-maya: short-term plan: increase analytics-api worker_count from 6 -> 8 as a canary, monitor queue. if safe, go to 10. also enable soft-circuit to return 503 for queries waiting > 15s. kubectl patch suggested: 
```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/analytics-api WORKER_COUNT=8
```
I'll open an incident and post the runbook.

ops-ryan: can do canary bump to 8 now, will watch queue_length and cpu. doing it in 2 mins.

support-jordan: I'll notify affected customers with workaround: narrow time range or refresh; apologizing and telling them we're investigating and ETA ~15-30m.

alyssa: thanks — please confirm when canary is up and if errors drop. tagging eng-ml for fallback UI change follow-up. :thumbsup:

eng-analytics-maya: canary up at 08:36 UTC, queue decreased to ~400 after scale. seeing error rate drop to ~0.5%. opening PR for circuit-breaker + soft-503. will follow up with postmortem once stable.

ops-ryan: confirmed metrics look healthy again, clickhouse ingest lag trending down. will keep monitoring for next 2 hours.

alyssa: I'll forward update to customers. thanks team.
